problem: The preceding R12 ellipse fix still refused finite major and normal components whenever their Euclidean norms exceeded binary64. In a direct scratch probe, normal=(1.5e308,1.5e308,0), major=(1,-1,0) and normal=(0,0,1), major=(1.5e308,1.5e308,0) each produced zero vertices, although the tested partial-arc vertices are finite. A tolerance-based 2D classifier also labeled very slightly tilted huge geometry as 2D even though its WCS Z displacement was around 1e295.

authority.scope: ELLIPSE uses WCS major/center and a plane normal; POLYLINE flag 8 selects 3D. Autodesk's 2D vertex API locates OCS Z on the owning polyline, so individual vertex Z cannot be relied on to preserve arbitrary WCS elevation.

implementation: Ellipse-specific DXF geometry validation and R12 tessellation normalize vectors by their largest finite component before computing directions. The tessellator factors the major scale, normalized norm, ratio, minor direction and each sampled sine via frexp/ldexp, avoiding premature overflow/underflow when the final minor contribution is representable. It refuses a nonzero component lost during vector normalization, an entirely underflowed minor axis, any nonfinite sampled vertex, and preserves the output destination. Exact XY normal and axis with zero elevation retain the classic 2D route; tilted or elevated geometry uses 3D vertices. The shared generic CIRCLE extrusion check is unchanged. For ratio>1, axis swapping now normalizes the source normal and major direction after component scaling, then computes each new axis component through exponent-separated multiplication. Preflight lets the transactional axis transform decide component representability rather than rejecting an overflowing scalar norm; any nonfinite or lost nonzero output component still refuses before emission. The sampled WCS coordinate accumulator now keeps center, major-axis and minor-axis terms as mantissa/exponent pairs, scales them to a shared exponent, and applies compensated summation before restoring the result. This preserves a finite coordinate when the minor-axis term alone exceeds DBL_MAX but its sum with the finite center does not.

validation.baseline: A scratch direct probe compiled with the c01e244d pre-follow-up drw_entities.cpp and linked to the local library printed normal=0 and major=0 vertices for the two independently chosen overflowing-norm cases. With the changed code the identical probe printed normal=2 and major=2.
validation.coverage: Generated direct and ASCII/Binary R12 partial/full controls verify analytically evaluated endpoints for overflowing-norm normal and major vectors, tilted 3D WCS flag/Z readback with and without extrusion, exact-XY 2D preservation, modern AC1027 ELLIPSE field readback, subnormal 1e-308 ratio with finite nonzero Z, and a partial arc with an unrepresentable full minor axis but representable sampled points. A full arc with a nonrepresentable sampled point and mixed-scale components lost during normalization refuse atomically and retry after correction. Existing ratio>1 overflow refusal and CIRCLE-normal behavior are retained. No fixtures are committed. The focused extreme-axis executable checks two generated partial ellipses whose sampled minor terms individually overflow binary64 but cancel against finite centers: ratio 1.5 with a 1.5e308 major axis and center -1.5e308, and the previously documented (1.5e308,1.5e308,0) major / (1,-1,0) normal / -5e307 Z-center case. It asserts the overflowing intermediate, both finite output vertices, and the independently scaled expected first coordinate. The ASCII/Binary R12 controls also cover ratio 1.1 with finite (1.3e308,1.3e308,0) major components (overflowing source norm) and a three-component normal that rotates the swapped axis so its norm exceeds DBL_MAX while each output component remains finite; fresh polyline readback matches direct source tessellation within the scaled tolerance. Existing nonrepresentable 1e308-by-4 axis refusal, destination preservation and corrected retry remain covered.
validation.focusedResult: 3/3 focused fast R12 ellipse geometry controls passed, including ASCII/Binary ratio-above-one output and readback with overflowing source and transformed norms.

limits: This is generated arithmetic and local codec/readback evidence, not native CAD rendering or a broad LibreCAD compatibility claim. The two selected generated shared-exponent cancellation cases pass; deeper cancellation and subnormal boundaries remain unqualified. The selected ratio>1 profile is qualified only for finite transformed axis components; if a component overflows or a nonzero component is lost to underflow, normalization refuses. Other extreme rounding combinations remain unqualified. A component that vanishes when normalizing a mixed-scale vector is conservatively refused; other extreme rounding boundaries remain unqualified. The ellipse-specific validation change also admits tested extreme finite ELLIPSE values on modern DXF input/output; local same-library readback does not prove native interpretation or rendering.
